question:
If $A = \{\text{letters of word INTEGRITY}\}$ and $B = \{\text{letters of word RECKONING}\}$, find

(i) $A \cup B$

(ii) $A \cap B$

(iii) $A - B$

(iv) $B - A$

Also verify that:

(a) $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$

(b) $n(A - B) = n(A \cup B) - n(B) = n(A) - n(A \cap B)$

(c) $n(B - A) = n(A \cup B) - n(A) = n(B) - n(A \cap B)$

(d) $n(A \cup B) = n(A - B) + n(B - A) + n(A \cap B)$

glassboxSteps.why: A set lists each letter only once; ignore repeats in the word.
Combine all unique letters from both sets.
Keep letters present in both sets.
Elements in the first set that are not in the second.
Substitute $n(A)=7$, $n(B)=8$, $n(A \cap B)=5$, $n(A \cup B)=10$.

explanation: Distinct letters: $A=\{I,N,T,E,G,R,Y\}$, $B=\{R,E,C,K,O,N,I,G\}$. Union 10, intersection 5, $A-B=\{T,Y\}$, $B-A=\{C,K,O\}$. Cardinality formula verified.

question: If  $ P = \{-1, 0, 1, 2, 5\} $ and  $ Q = \{3, 5, 7\} $, then  $ P \cup Q $ is

glassboxSteps.why: $P \cup Q$ contains every element from $P$ and from $Q$, without repeating shared elements.
Start with all of $P$, then add $3$ and $7$ from $Q$ ($5$ is already listed).

explanation: Union lists all elements once: $\{-1,0,1,2,3,5,7\}$ (Option C). $\{5\}$ is the intersection, not the union.

question: If $A$ and $B$ are two sets, then $A - B$ is defined as

glassboxSteps.why: Set difference keeps elements that belong to $A$ but not to $B$.
glassboxSteps.math: A-B=\{x \mid x \in A \text{ and } x \notin B\}

glassboxSteps.why: Option A is union; Option D is $B-A$.

explanation: $A-B$ means elements in $A$ only: $\{x \mid x \in A \text{ and } x \notin B\}$ (Option C).

question: If $A$ is any set, then $A \cap \phi$ is

glassboxSteps.why: $\phi$ has no elements.
No element can belong to both $A$ and an empty set.

explanation: Intersecting any set with the empty set gives $\phi$ (Option B).

question: $A\cap\xi$ is same as

glassboxSteps.why: $\xi$ contains every element under consideration; $A \subseteq \xi$.
Every element of $A$ is already in $\xi$.

explanation: Intersecting a set with the universal set returns the set itself: $A$ (Option A).

question: If $\xi = \mathrm{W}$ and $\mathrm{A} = \{x \mid x \in \mathrm{W} \text{ and } x \leq 10\}$, then $\mathrm{A}'$ is

glassboxSteps.why: $\xi=\mathrm{W}=\{0,1,2,3,\ldots\}$ and $A=\{x \in \mathrm{W}: x \leq 10\}$.
Elements of $\xi$ not in $A$.

explanation: Whole numbers greater than 10 form the complement: $\{x \in \mathrm{W}: x \geq 11\}$ (Option D).

question: If $\xi = \{x \mid x \in \mathbb{N}, x \leq 12\}$, $A = \{x \mid x \text{ is a multiple of } 3\}$ and $B = \{x \mid x \text{ is a multiple of } 4\}$, then $A \cap B$ is

glassboxSteps.why: Natural numbers from 1 to 12.
List multiples within $\xi$.
Common multiples of 3 and 4 in $\xi$.

explanation: Only 12 is a common multiple of 3 and 4 up to 12. Since $\mathbb{N}$ starts at 1, 0 is excluded (Option C).

question: If $\xi = \{ \text{all digits in our number system} \}$, $A = \{ x \mid x \text{ is prime} \}$ and $B = \{ x \mid x \text{ is even} \}$, then $B - A$ is

glassboxSteps.why: Digits are 0–9; 0 and 1 are not prime.
Even digits except those also prime (remove 2).

explanation: Even digits minus the prime digit 2 gives $\{0,4,6,8\}$ (Option B).
